title: Day 30 · Week 4, Day 2 — Physiology: the gland that keeps the lights on — the corpus luteum, the hormone that rescues it, and where the tiredness, the sore breasts and the bathroom trips come from
summary: The first Physiology episode, and the machinery is your partner's, because your baby (about 0.4 mm, Carnegie stage 7, making the first blood islands in the yolk sac) has none yet. The corpus luteum: the grape-sized remnant of the follicle that normally switches off after about 14 days (that switching off is a period), rescued this month by hCG, which binds the LH receptor. Csapo's luteectomy studies showing the pregnancy depends on it until about seven weeks, and the luteal-placental shift between seven and ten weeks. What progesterone does: holds the uterine lining, relaxes smooth muscle (bloating, constipation, early heartburn, falling blood pressure) and sedates via allopregnanolone at the GABA-A receptor. The numbers on the symptoms: 44.4% of 5,079 Generation R women tired every day vs 33.6% with daily nausea; longer but lighter, more broken sleep on home polysomnography by 11–12 weeks; half of women symptomatic by Day 36 and 89% by the end of week 8, with symptoms a poor signal either way. Breast changes, and why the bathroom trips come from a ~50% rise in kidney filtration rather than the bladder. hCG nudging the thyroid (18% low TSH in the first trimester). How to read an hCG pair if one is ever drawn, the conservative ultrasound criteria for nonviability, why a single progesterone level says little — and the PROMISE and PRISM trials (836 and 4,153 women) that found routine progesterone does not help most pregnancies, plus the subgroup (72% vs 57% live births) behind NICE's 2021 recommendation for women who bleed and have miscarried before.
action: Tonight, pick one recurring evening job that is currently hers (dishes, the dog, lunches, an older child's bedtime) and take it over for the rest of the first trimester — tell her which one, out loud. Put a night light in the hallway between the bed and the bathroom.
